summary: This Wikipedia-derived note on Oklahoma City covers its status as the state capital and largest city, with population figures, geography, history from the 1889 Land Run, and the MAPS redevelopment program. It also describes the area's universities, the Oklahoma City Thunder and other sports venues, major employers, and local broadcasting history including WKY.
one_line: Overview of Oklahoma City: its population, geography, 1889 settlement, MAPS redevelopment, universities, Thunder basketball, and broadcasting history.
key_facts: Oklahoma City is the capital and largest city of Oklahoma and the county seat of Oklahoma County; it ranks 27th among U.S. cities in population.
The 2014 population estimate for Oklahoma City was 620,602, the largest ever recorded, and the first Oklahoma city to exceed 600,000 residents.
The Oklahoma City metropolitan area had 1,322,429 people in 2014, and the Oklahoma City-Shawnee Combined Statistical Area had 1,459,758.
Oklahoma City is the eighth-largest U.S. city by land area and the largest whose government is not consolidated with a county or borough.
Oklahoma City was settled on April 22, 1889, in the "Land Run" of the "Unassigned Lands"; about 10,000 homesteaders settled the area and the population doubled between 1890 and 1900.
The capital moved from Guthrie to Oklahoma City soon after Oklahoma gained statehood in 1907.
Patience Latting was elected Mayor in 1971, becoming the city's first female mayor and the first woman to be mayor of a U.S. city with over 350,000 residents.
The Oklahoma City Thunder have played in the city since the 2008–09 season, when owner Clayton Bennett moved the franchise from Seattle; they play at Chesapeake Energy Arena.
The Thunder won 59 games in 2014 and have won Northwest Division titles every year since 2009; stars include Russell Westbrook, Kevin Durant and Serge Ibaka, with first-year head coach Billy Donovan.
The 1993 Metropolitan Area Projects (MAPS) program rebuilt downtown with a ballpark, central library, and a Bricktown canal, and drew over $3 billion in private investment as of 2010.
May 2015 was the city's wettest month since records began in 1890, with 19.48 inches of rainfall.

WKY Radio, licensed in 1921, was the first radio station west of the Mississippi River and the third in the U.S.; WKY-TV went on the air in 1949 and was the first independently owned U.S. station to broadcast in color.
As of the 2010 census, the city had 579,999 people, 230,233 households and 144,120 families.
The city is roughly bisected by the North Canadian River (renamed the Oklahoma River within city limits) and has three large lakes: Hefner, Overholser and Stanley Draper.
